case_title: Ram Chandra Bhagat v. State of Jharkhand
accused_victim_relationship: Cohabiting partner (not lawfully married); accused had promised marriage
evidence_type: Documentary (agreement, Special Marriage application, voter lists) and oral testimony of five witnesses
confession: Written agreement (Ex.2) in which accused admitted living as married with victim; relied on by Misra J. Katju J noted the accused disputed the agreement.
aggravating_circumstances: Nine years of deception-based cohabitation; two children; accused later drove victim out
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.493 IPC; sentence not stated in judgment
high_court_outcome: Conviction under s.493 IPC upheld in Criminal Revision No. 788 of 2005 (order dated 08.09.2005)
neutral_facts: The victim worked in a government agriculture office in the early 1980s when she began an intimate relationship with the accused. The two lived together as a couple for about nine years and had two children. The victim alleged that the accused had assured her of marriage and had signed a written agreement to that effect dated 4 June 1990; the accused disputed that agreement. Evidence presented included an application made by the accused to a Special Marriage Officer, dated 13 April 1982, seeking information about marriage under the Special Marriage Act. A further document dated 4 June 1982, written on stamp paper, recorded that the accused was living a normal family life as a married couple with the victim and that the victim was the accused's wife. Voter lists for 1984, 1988 and 1993 for the village where the couple lived showed the victim as the accused's wife. Five witnesses testified that the two lived together as husband and wife at several places of the accused's official posting, including a block in Hazaribagh district, and that a son was born during the cohabitation. The accused was also said to have celebrated the birth of the couple's daughter and son with friends. A witness described a local social custom under which a woman who lives in a man's house for a long period is deemed to be his wife. No marriage ceremony had been performed between them. The accused later refused to accept the victim as wife and drove her out of the house.
offence_severity: Imprisonment up to ten years, and fine; no minimum stated
number_of_offences: 1 charged; 0 finally decided (split bench, referred to Chief Justice of India)
motive: alleged: inducing cohabitation through a promise of marriage
key_evidence_accepted: Special Marriage application (Ex.3); marriage agreement (Ex.2); voter lists 1984, 1988, 1993 (Ex.6, 6/1, 6/2); oral testimony of PW-1, PW-3, PW-4, PW-5, PW-6 (Misra J)
witness_credibility: Witnesses supported the relationship as husband and wife; assessed as credible by Misra J. Katju J did not address witness credibility.
post_offence_conduct: Refused to accept victim as wife and drove her out of the house
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 08.09.2005; Supreme Court: 24.11.2010
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: Deba Prasad Mukherjee; State/respondent: Ratan Kumar Chaudhari
investigation_status: Not stated; case proceeded to trial and conviction by trial court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.493 IPC; first appellate court: convicted; High Court: conviction upheld (08.09.2005); Supreme Court: split verdict, referred to Chief Justice of India
defence_argument: Not stated in judgment; accused disputed the marriage agreement
legal_principle_applied: Katju J: strict construction; no assurance of future marriage means no belief of existing marriage, so s.493 not met. Misra J: three ingredients (deceit, inducement of belief of lawful marriage, cohabitation as result); no ritual or statutory ceremony required.
precedent_relied_upon: Moideenkutty Haji v. Kunhikoya, AIR 1987 Kerala 184; Dr. A.N. Mukerji v. State, AIR 1969 Allahabad 489 (both cited by Katju J)
other_sentence_order: Referral of the matter to the Chief Justice of India for placement before another Bench due to split opinion
